card.name: Linking words before a next descriptive term
card.fires_on: Small linking or auxiliary words (including, show, a, even, have, and) that sit right before an expected descriptor, such as a result, a comparative or a named condition, in drug-label text.

modes.label: Including before a condition
modes.description: The word including introduces a list of toxicities after a named drug effect.
modes.example: Methotrexate-induced lung disease,<< including>> acute or chronic interstitial pneumonitis

modes.label: Show before a finding
modes.description: The verb show comes right before a test result such as mutagenic potential.
modes.example: Diclofenac sodium did not<< show>> mutagenic activity in in vitro point

modes.label: Before a comparative
modes.description: A small word such as a, even or have comes before a comparative like more rapid, more gradual or greater.
modes.example: Some patients may benefit from an<< even>> more gradual discontinuation.

card.writes: It seems to push toward Chinese verb-like words and away from words meaning significant or marked, so no clear overall effect on label text.
card.plain: It fires on small connecting words that come just before a describing word or result in a label sentence.
